issues.failure_explanation: If every component of the alleged minimizer has magnitude exactly $\mu$, then $\cI_1\cup\cI_2$ is empty, so the displayed minimum defining $\rho$ is undefined. The proof therefore does not cover an allowed contradiction case.

failure_location.quote: Define $\rho := \tfrac{1}{2} \min_{i \in \cI_1 \cup \cI_2} \{||\wvx_i| - \mu|\}$. For any $0 < \epsilon < \rho$, the perturbation $\wvx \pm \epsilon \vv$ remains feasible.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle $\cI_1\cup\cI_2=\varnothing$ separately, or choose an independent sufficiently small positive perturbation bound that also controls the breakpoint coordinates.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exclusion of breakpoint-valued constrained minimizers, and the later constrained optimality result insofar as it invokes that exclusion, lack a complete proof for this degenerate case.
issues.title: Degenerate all-breakpoint case is not covered by the differentiability proof
issues.why_classification: The omitted case can be covered by a short local modification of the perturbation argument without changing the theorem or its assumptions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, $\wvx$ is a local minimizer, proving sufficiency.
Theorem  \ref{linearoptcond} establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}.

issues.failure_explanation: The sufficiency argument fixes the active regions and proves only local minimality. The conditions do not imply global minimality: with $m=1,n=2$, $A=(1,1)$, $b=3$, and $\mu=1$, the feasible point $(3/2,3/2)$ avoids the breakpoints and satisfies the stationarity condition with multiplier zero, but has objective $2$, whereas $(0,3)$ is feasible with objective $1$. The convergence theorem then uses the same local condition to call a limit point a minimizer. Indeed, for $A=(1,10,10)$, $b=2$, $\mu=1$, and initialization $x=(2,0,0)$, $\omega=(1,0,0)$, the BCD iteration is fixed with objective $1<\operatorname{spark}(A)=2$, while $(0,0.2,0)$ has objective $0.04$.

issues.failure_explanation: Away from the breakpoints, the displayed equation is a first-order condition and gives local minimality within a fixed active pattern, not global minimality of the nonconvex objective. For example, take $A=(1,10)$, $b=2$, $\mu=1$, and any $\alpha>0$. The point $(2,0)$ has zero residual, avoids the breakpoints, and satisfies the displayed equation, but its objective is $1$, while $(0,0.2)$ has zero residual and objective $0.04$. Starting the BCD method at $(2,0)$ with $\omega=(1,0)$ leaves it fixed and satisfies the theorem's initial bound $1<\operatorname{spark}(A)=2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State only a local optimality characterization and weaken Theorem \ref{convergalg2} to convergence to a local or coordinatewise minimizer. Retaining global convergence would require new structural assumptions or a different global argument.
issues.overall_effect: The global part of the noisy optimality characterization and the claimed convergence of noisy BCD to the model minimizer are invalid; nonglobal fixed points satisfy all stated initialization requirements.
issues.title: Noisy stationarity likewise does not imply global minimality

issues.failure_explanation: When $|x_i|=\mu$, both $\omega_i=0$ and $\omega_i=1$ give the same component value $1$ in $\cQ_\mu$. Thus $\cH_\mu(x)$ is a selected minimizer, not the entire argmin set, and the proof's claimed unique threshold rule is false at equality. The minimum-value identity remains valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace equality to the argmin by membership and explicitly describe the two-way tie at components satisfying $|x_i|=\mu$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the exact argmin characterization is wrong; the chosen update $\cH_\mu$ is still a legitimate minimizer and the surrogate-value equality survives.
issues.title: Surrogate minimizer is nonunique at the threshold
issues.why_classification: A local set-valued correction preserves the surrogate reformulation and all chosen updates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $m=\mathrm{spark}(A)-1\leq\mathrm{rank}(A)\leq m$, the matrices $A_{\cI^{j}_{1}}^\top A_{\cI^{j}_{1}}$ and $A_{\cI^{j}_{2}}A_{\cI^{j}_{2}}^\top$ are invertible.

issues.failure_explanation: From $m<n$ and $|\cI_1^j|\le m$ one obtains only $|\cI_2^j|\ge n-m$, not $n-m>m$. For allowed dimensions such as $n=m+1$, $\cI_1^j$ may contain $m$ indices and $\cI_2^j$ only one, so the $m\times m$ matrix $A_{\cI_2^j}A_{\cI_2^j}^\top$ is singular when $m>1$. Full spark does not cure the shortage of columns, and the prescribed update is then undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either impose and maintain a condition ensuring $|\cI_2^j|\ge m$, such as an appropriate dimensional restriction, or replace the displayed inverse formula with a KKT-based solver valid for every full-spark active set allowed by $|\cI_1^j|<\operatorname{spark}(A)$.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm \ref{BCD} is not well defined for all dimensions and iterates admitted by the noise-free convergence theorem, so that theorem cannot universally refer to a generated sequence.
issues.title: Noise-free BCD inverse can be singular under the stated spark assumptions
issues.why_classification: A comparable algorithm can survive, but repair requires an additional regime restriction or a nontrivial alternative linear-system update rather than a routine algebraic correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Because $m<n$, the denominator $m-n+\operatorname{card}(\mathcal K+1)$ is nonpositive whenever $\operatorname{card}(\mathcal K+1)\le n-m$. No condition in the algorithm prevents this. If the set contains a nonzero component but has cardinality below $n-m$, the radicand is negative; at equality the denominator is zero. Hence the required update is not a real-valued operation on admitted iterates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a mathematically justified branch for nonpositive denominators or replace the formula with a well-defined positive decreasing update, and separately establish any claimed active-set invertibility property.
issues.overall_effect: The continuation procedure may fail to produce the next threshold, so its claimed numerical stabilization strategy is not an executable algorithm for general inputs.
issues.title: Continuation update can take the square root of a negative quantity
issues.why_classification: The outer strategy is repairable without changing the underlying BCD model, but the source does not supply a routine forced correction to the invalid update or its asserted stability rationale.
